subsystems.name: Sample collection
subsystems.role: draws a consistent drop of capillary blood from a fingertip.

subsystems.name: Microfluidic cartridge
subsystems.role: meters, dilutes and mixes the blood with reagents without a lab technician.

subsystems.name: Detection unit
subsystems.role: converts a biomarker's concentration into a measurable signal.
parts: optical sensor for colorimetric or fluorescence assays

subsystems.name: Reader electronics
subsystems.role: runs the assay and digitises the result.
parts: potentiostat or light source and detector

subsystems.name: Software and algorithms
subsystems.role: turns raw signals into results, trends and alerts.

subsystems.name: Quality control
subsystems.role: keeps results comparable across cartridges, temperatures and users.

buildSteps.title: Choose the biomarker panel
buildSteps.detail: Decide which analytes the cartridge will measure and in what range, because this determines the chemistry and sample volume.

buildSteps.title: Develop the assay chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Select enzymes, antibodies or chemical reactions that produce an electrical or optical signal proportional to each biomarker.

buildSteps.title: Design the microfluidic cartridge
buildSteps.detail: Lay out channels, valves and reagent chambers so a single drop is split, diluted and delivered to each sensor reliably.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise the reagents
buildSteps.detail: Dry or freeze-dry the reagents so the cartridge can be stored at room temperature and still work months later.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the cartridge
buildSteps.detail: Mould or laminate plastic layers, deposit electrodes and reagent spots, and seal the fluidic paths.

buildSteps.title: Build the reader
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the electronics and optics, write firmware to run the assay sequence, and pair it with a phone app.

buildSteps.title: Validate against laboratory methods
buildSteps.detail: Compare results with venous blood analysed on standard lab instruments across many users and conditions.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture under medical-device rules
buildSteps.detail: Set up clean-room production, batch testing and regulatory approval for home use.

prerequisites.why: separating plasma from a tiny fingerprick sample and avoiding bubbles or clots is difficult outside a lab.
they underpin today's home glucose and pregnancy tests and can be adapted to more analytes.
many proteins and enzymes degrade unless carefully preserved for room-temperature storage.
fingerprick collection is routine, though capillary blood can differ from venous blood.
home results must be accurate enough to guide care, which requires large trials and device approval.
trends over time are more useful than single readings, but algorithms must avoid false reassurance.

pathway.milestone: single-analyte home tests such as glucose meters and coagulation monitors
pathway.unlocks: routine self-monitoring for a few specific conditions.

pathway.milestone: multi-biomarker cartridges for cholesterol, HbA1c, kidney and liver markers
pathway.unlocks: regular screening and chronic-disease tracking without clinic visits.

pathway.milestone: integration with telehealth and electronic health records
pathway.unlocks: clinicians can act on home results remotely.
early detection of deterioration and tighter management of long-term conditions.
